arxiv-1909-07094.title: Beam impact tests of a prototype target for the Beam Dump Facility at CERN: experimental setup and preliminary analysis of the online results
arxiv-1909-07094.creator: E. Lopez Sola, M. Calviani, O. Aberle, C. Ahdida, P. Avigni, M. Battistin, L. Bianchi, S. Burger, J. Busom Descarrega, J. Canhoto Espadanal, E. Cano-Pleite, M. Casolino, M.A. Fraser, S. Gilardoni, S. Girod, J-L. Grenard, D. Grenier, M. Guinchard, C. Hessler, R. Jacobsson, M. Lamont, A. Ortega Rolo,
arxiv-1909-07094.description: Abstract The Beam Dump Facility (BDF) is a project for a new facility at CERN dedicated to high intensity beam dump and fixed target experiments. Currently in its design phase, the first aim of the facility is to search for Light Dark Matter and Hidden Sector models with the Search for Hidden Particles (SHiP) experiment.

arxiv-2204-07765.title: Experimental violation of the Leggett-Garg inequality with a single-spin system
arxiv-2204-07765.creator: Maimaitiyiming Tusun, Wei Cheng, Zihua Chai, Yang Wu, Ya Wang, Xing Rong, Jiangfeng Du
arxiv-2204-07765.description: Abstract Investigation the boundary between quantum mechanical description and classical realistic view is of fundamental importance. The Leggett-Garg inequality provides a criterion to distinguish between quantum systems and classical systems, and can be used to prove the macroscopic superposition state. A larger upper bound of the LG function can be obtained in a multi-level system.

arxiv-2210-06079.title: Birational Invariance in Punctured Log Gromov-Witten Theory
arxiv-2210-06079.creator: Samuel Johnston
arxiv-2210-06079.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Samuel Johnston. Given a log smooth scheme ( X , D ) (X,D) , and a log étale modification ( X ~ , D ~ ) → ( X , D ) (\tilde{X},\tilde{D})\rightarrow(X,D) , we relate the punctured Gromov-Witten theory of ( X ~ , D ~ ) (\tilde{X},\tilde{D}) to the punctured Gromov-Witten theory of ( X , D ) (X,D) , generalizing results of Abramovich and Wise in the non-punctured setting in [ AW13 ] .

arxiv-2303-12835.title: Compact and Quiescent Circumgalactic Medium and Ly α \alpha Halos around Extremely Red Quasars (ERQs) 2023 Compact and Quiescent Circumgalactic Medium and Ly α \alpha Halos around Extremely Red Quasars (ERQs) – References
arxiv-2303-12835.creator: Jarred Gillette, Marie Wingyee Lau, Fred Hamann, Serena Perrotta, David S. N. Rupke, Dominika Wylezalek, Nadia L. Zakamska, Andrey Vayner
arxiv-2303-12835.description: Abstract Red quasars may represent a young stage of galaxy evolution that provide important feedback to their host galaxies. We are studying a population of extremely red quasars (ERQs) with exceptionally fast and powerful outflows, at median redshift z z = 2.6.

arxiv-2403-09285.title: THÖR-MAGNI: A Large-scale Indoor Motion Capture Recording of Human Movement and Robot Interaction
arxiv-2403-09285.creator: Tim Schreiter * \affilnum 1, Tiago Rodrigues de Almeida * \affilnum 1, Yufei Zhu \affilnum 1, Eduardo Gutierrez Maestro \affilnum 1, Lucas Morillo-Mendez \affilnum 6, Andrey Rudenko \affilnum 2, Luigi Palmieri \affilnum 2, Tomasz P. Kucner \affilnum 3,4, Martin Magnusson \affilnum 1, Achim J. Lilien
arxiv-2403-09285.description: Abstract We present a new large dataset of indoor human and robot navigation and interaction, called THÖR-MAGNI, that is designed to facilitate research on social navigation: e.g., modelling and predicting human motion, analyzing goal-oriented interactions between humans and robots, and investigating visual attention in a social interaction context.

arxiv-2408-01729.title: A Survey on Robotic Prosthetics: Neuroprosthetics, Soft Actuators, and Control Strategies
arxiv-2408-01729.creator: Jyothish K. J, Subhankar Mishra
arxiv-2408-01729.description: Abstract . The field of robotics is a quickly evolving feat of technology that accepts contributions from various genres of science. Neuroscience, Physiology, Chemistry, Material science, Computer science, and the wide umbrella of mechatronics have all simultaneously contributed to many innovations in the prosthetic applications of robotics.

arxiv-2501-03569.title: What Does a Software Engineer Look Like? Exploring Societal Stereotypes in LLMs
arxiv-2501-03569.creator: Muneera Bano, Hashini Gunatilake, Rashina Hoda
arxiv-2501-03569.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have rapidly gained popularity and are being embedded into professional applications due to their capabilities in generating human-like content. However, unquestioned reliance on their outputs and recommendations can be problematic as LLMs can reinforce societal biases and stereotypes.

arxiv-2503-01385.title: Q-NL Verifier: Leveraging Synthetic Data for Robust Knowledge Graph Question Answering
arxiv-2503-01385.creator: Tim Schwabe, Louisa Siebel, Patrik Valach, Maribel Acosta
arxiv-2503-01385.description: Abstract Question answering (QA) requires accurately aligning user questions with structured queries—a process often limited by the scarcity of high-quality query–natural language (Q–NL) pairs. To overcome this, we present Q-NL Verifier, an approach to generating high-quality synthetic pairs of queries and NL translations.

arxiv-2504-14937.title: Causal DAG Summarization (Full Version)
arxiv-2504-14937.creator: Anna Zeng, Michael Cafarella, Batya Kenig, Markos Markakis, Brit Youngmann, Babak Salimi
arxiv-2504-14937.description: Abstract . Causal inference aids researchers in discovering cause-and-effect relationships, leading to scientific insights. Accurate causal estimation requires identifying confounding variables to avoid false discoveries. Pearl’s causal model uses causal DAGs to identify confounding variables, but incorrect DAGs can lead to unreliable causal conclusions. However, for high dimensional data, the causal DAGs are often complex beyond human verifiability.

arxiv-2507-16639.title: Benchmarking pig detection and tracking under diverse and challenging conditions
arxiv-2507-16639.creator: Jonathan Henrich, Christian Post, Maximilian Zilke, Parth Shiroya, Emma Chanut, Amir Mollazadeh Yamchi, Ramin Yahyapour, Thomas Kneib, Imke Traulsen
arxiv-2507-16639.description: Abstract To ensure animal welfare and effective management in pig farming, monitoring individual behavior is a crucial prerequisite. While monitoring tasks have traditionally been carried out manually, advances in machine learning have made it possible to collect individualized information in an increasingly automated way.

arxiv-2508-06307.title: Quarkonium Parton Shower in Herwig 7
arxiv-2508-06307.creator: M.R. Masouminia, P. Richardson
arxiv-2508-06307.description: Abstract We present the implementation of a fully automated quarkonium parton shower in Herwig 7 , based on non-relativistic QCD (NRQCD) factorisation with spin-colour projections. The framework systematically incorporates colour-singlet and colour-octet production mechanisms, gluon fragmentation, and diquark production processes. Perturbative short-distance coefficients are combined with non-perturbative NRQCD matrix elements to simulate heavy-quark bound state formation.

europmc-pmc3257222.description: Background People with eating disorders (ED) frequently present with inflexible behaviours, including eating related issues which contribute to the maintenance of the illness. Small scale studies point to difficulties with cognitive set-shifting as a basis. Using larger scale st

pmc-10559987.title: Comparative metataxonamic analyses of seeds and leaves of traditional varieties and hybrids of cucumber (Cucumis sativus L.) reveals distinct and core microbiome
pmc-10559987.creator: Botlagunta Navya, Subramanian Babu
pmc-10559987.description: Profiling the endophytic microbiome of different tissues and varieties of agricultural crops can help to understand i) the tissue specific and varietal specific microbes associated with the plants ii) their potential role in growth, stress tolerance, disease resistance, and yield of the plants.

pmc-10601385.title: Staminal hairs increase pollinator attraction and pollination accuracy in Tradescantia fluminensis (Commelinaceae)
pmc-10601385.creator: Deng-Fei Li, Yi-Dan Chen, Zhen Liu, Ai-Ting Liang, Ju Tang, Xian-Chun Yan
pmc-10601385.description: Staminal hairs are the particular appendages of stamens, which may affect pollinator foraging behaviour and pollen transfer. However, experimental evidence of the functions of staminal hairs in pollination remains scarce. Here, we conducted staminal hair manipulation experiments in Tradescantia fluminensis (Commelinaceae) to investigate their effects on visitation and pollen transfer by bees.

pmc-11439936.title: Biochar improves growth and physiology of Swietenia macrophylla king in contaminated soil by copper
pmc-11439936.creator: Raphael Leone da Cruz Ferreira, Dayse Gonzaga Braga, Vitor Resende do Nascimento, Camilly Barbosa da Silva, Anne Cristina Barbosa Alves, Joyce Adriany da Costa Cabral, Flávio José Rodrigues Cruz, Ana Ecídia de Araújo Brito, Glauco Andre dos Santos Nogueira, Luma Castro de Souza, Eniel David Cruz, Câ
pmc-11439936.description: The production of açaí seed waste from the commercial and extractive exploitation of the Euterpe oleraceae palm tree is a serious problem that contributes to environmental contamination and production of greenhouse gases, a fact that suggests the need for an environmentally correct destination for this waste produced on a large scale.

pmc-11484868.title: Advanced chelate technology-based trace minerals reduce inflammation and oxidative stress in Eimeria-infected broilers by modulating NF-kB and Nrf2 pathways
pmc-11484868.creator: Nasim Biabani, Kamran Taherpour, Hossein Ali Ghasemi, Mohammad Akbari Gharaei, Maryam Hafizi, Mohammad Hassan Nazaran
pmc-11484868.description: This study investigated the effects of substituting inorganic trace minerals (ITM) with advanced chelate technology-based TM (ACTM) in broiler chicken feed on productive performance, metabolic profile, humoral immunity, antioxidant status, and modulation of NF-kB and Nrf2 signaling pathways in mixed Eimeria species exposure.

pmc-11505716.title: A Machine Learning Assisted Non-Enzymatic Electrochemical Biosensor to Detect Urea Based on Multi-Walled Carbon Nanotube Functionalized with Copper Oxide Micro-Flowers
pmc-11505716.creator: Jitendra B. Zalke, Manish L. Bhaiyya, Pooja A. Jain, Devashree N. Sakharkar, Jayu Kalambe, Nitin P. Narkhede, Mangesh B. Thakre, Dinesh R. Rotake, Madhusudan B. Kulkarni, Shiv Govind Singh
pmc-11505716.description: Detecting urea is crucial for diagnosing related health conditions and ensuring timely medical intervention. The addition of machine learning (ML) technologies has completely changed the field of biochemical sensing, providing enhanced accuracy and reliability. In the present work, an ML-assisted screen-printed, flexible, electrochemical, non-enzymatic biosensor was proposed to quantify urea concentrations.

pmc-12608898.title: Multiscale Prediction for Mechanical and Thermal Properties of Needled Composites Considering Pore and Their Application
pmc-12608898.creator: Shiyong Sun, Junlong Wang, Hailin Li, Rui Yang, Liming Zhou, Aniello Riccio
pmc-12608898.description: Needled ceramic composites have great application prospects for high-temperature structural components. However, due to the manufacturing defects, the properties of the composite show significant dispersion, which poses great challenges for predicting the service life. Firstly, X-ray computed tomography was used to determine the pores in the composites, and multiscale models considering the pores were established.

pmc-13326089.title: Multi-omics uncovers the pleiotropic genetic mechanisms linking MASLD and cardiometabolic syndromes
pmc-13326089.creator: Kangjia Yin, Cao Zhang, Bing Liu, Ruyun Xu, Jing Zeng, Mohammed Eslam, Jing Ni
pmc-13326089.description: Background Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome are interrelated conditions with shared pathophysiological features; however, the genetic architecture underlying their relationship has not been fully elucidated. Deciphering this shared genetic basis holds promise for advancing mechanistic insights and therapeutic discovery.MethodsWe performed an integrated genome-wide cross-trait analysis using GWAS summary statistics for MASLD and 38 CKM traits.

pmc-13356091.title: Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis of Glecaprevir and Pibrentasvir in Pediatric Patients ≥ 3 to < 18 Years of Age with Genotypes 1–6 Chronic Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) Infection
pmc-13356091.creator: Neha Thakre, Denise Beck, Ahmed M. Saeed, Doerthe Eckert, Mong-Jen Chen, Wei Liu, Hoi Kei Lon, Nael M. Mostafa, Sven Mensing
pmc-13356091.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMavyret, a combination medication of glecaprevir (GLE) and pibrentasvir (PIB), is approved to treat chronic and acute hepatitis C virus (HCV) (genotypes 1–6) infection in adults and pediatric patients ≥ 3 years old.

pmc-13446103.title: Plasma proteomic profile of inflammatory depressive symptoms
pmc-13446103.creator: Filip Ängeby, Filip Ventorp, Miranda Stiernborg, Klara Suneson, Gustav Söderberg Veibäck, Jesper Lindahl, Johanna Tjernberg, Darya Ståhl, Jonas Berge, Catharina Lavebratt, Daniel Lindqvist

pmc-13475970.title: Uneven development of intangible cultural heritage: A spatial analysis of traditional drama in Southwestern China
pmc-13475970.creator: Yun Qin, Zhiyi Zeng, Keyao Qin, Jiexi Xiong, Xiang Yan
pmc-13475970.description: Intangible cultural heritage (ICH) exhibits pronounced spatial unevenness, yet the spatial patterns and driving mechanisms of traditional drama as a form of living performing heritage remain insufficiently understood. Taking Southwest China as a case, this study analyzes 257 traditional drama ICH items, comprising 54 national-level and 203 provincial-level items.

uslaw-usc-t36-s151910.title: 36 U.S.C. § 151910 — Liability for acts of officers and agents
uslaw-usc-t36-s151910.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t36-s151910.description: United States Code, Title 36 (Patriotic And National Observances, Ceremonies, And Organizations); Part B (Organizations); Chapter 1519 (National Fund For Medical Education). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The corporation is liable for the acts of its officers and agents acting within the scope of their authority.
